newsitem.title: INDIA: Cricket-Adams wrecks Indian middle order.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Adams wrecks Indian middle order.

text.p: South Africa's left-arm spinner Paul Adams ran through the Indian middle order to leave the home team struggling on the first day of the third and final cricket test on Sunday.
Adams claimed three wickets in the space of 15 deliveries as India slumped from a sound start to finish the day at 204 for six.
India's hopes of posting a respectable score on a treacherous track, where the ball spun wildly and stayed low, depended on skipper Sachin Tendulkar.
Tendulkar was not out on 43 with Anil Kumble on five.
Indian openers Nayan Mongia (41) and Woorkeri Raman (57) put on 76 before both fell to Brian McMillan who bowled Mongia through the gate and had Raman caught in the gully off an outswinger.

Left-handed Raman, recalled to the test squad after nearly four years in oblivion, was India's top scorer and the partnership was India's highest for the first wicket in seven tests against South Africa.
South African skipper Hansie Cronje trapped Saurav Ganguly leg before for 39 to make it 160 for three soon after tea.
Then Adams swiftly removed Rahul Dravid (7), Mohammed Azharuddin (5) and Sunil Joshi (0), ending the day on 3-31 off 14 overs. McMillan finished with 2-40.
Much now rests on Tendulkar who became the youngest batsman to score 3,000 runs in test cricket when he reached 10 in his innings on Sunday.
Tendulkar, playing his 45th test, achieved the landmark aged 23 years 228 days. The record was previously held by Javed Miandad of Pakistan who attained the target at the age of 24 years 280 days.
